project.name: Formation Zero
project.tagline: Teaching a computer to watch NFL coaches film.

phase.name: Ingestion and the NFL API
phase.plain: Planning is closed. The first build milestone gets the film and the official data into a shape the vision code can eat: a modern Python runtime, a cheaper copy of the video, one clip per play per angle, a Python client for the NFL's own API, and version 1 of the play record schema so clients can integrate before any vision runs.

what_it_is: Every NFL game is filmed from two high angles that show all 22 players at once. Coaches call it All-22. It is the film they actually study.

Formation Zero watches that film with computer vision: it finds the players and the ball on every frame, works out where each one is standing in real yards, and turns a video into a spreadsheet of positions.

From that spreadsheet it reads football: the formation, the personnel on the field, who lined up where, who moved before the snap. Then you can ask it questions in plain English, and it can redraw any play from above, or from any angle, like a video game replay.

end_state.title: How it will work when it's done
steps: You hand it a game film and tell it which game it is (season, week, teams).
It pulls the official play-by-play for that game from the NFL's API on its own.
It cuts the film into plays, finds every player and the ball on every frame, and works out where each one stood in real yards.
It reads the football: formation, personnel, motion, routes, coverage, the tackle. One JSON record per play, every field with a source and a confidence.
Everything lands in the database. From there: the bird's-eye view, the 3D replay, the chat, the API for clients, and the exports.
Runs on a laptop in about an hour per game to start; on a server later. Only the hard plays cost money, and that is capped.

next_up: Get the NFL API credentials onto this machine and test the port against a real payload (the last milestone 1 item).
Run probe, proxy and film-window detection on the real demo film once it is on disk.
Milestone 2: measure SAM 3 throughput on the M4, then the labelling teacher.
